chunks: 1269 – Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

"If you enter a town while intending to stay for ten days, then perform the prayer in full when you arrive. If you intend to stay less than ten days, then shorten it. And if you remain saying, 'Tomorrow I will leave,' and 'the day after tomorrow,' and have not resolved upon ten days, then shorten the prayer for as long as there is between you and a month; when the month is complete, then perform the prayer in full."
He said: I said, "If I enter a town on the first day of the month of Ramaḍān, and I do not intend to stay for ten days?" He said, "Shorten the prayer and break the fast."

I said, "If I remain like that, saying, 'Tomorrow' or 'the day after tomorrow,' should I break the fast for the entire month and shorten the prayer?" He said, "Yes. This is one rule: when you shorten the prayer, you break the fast; and when you break the fast, you shorten the prayer."

key_terms.أَفْطِرْ: break the fast, meaning do not observe the fast while under the travel ruling
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: residing or staying in a place
key_terms.شَهْرٍ: a month, after which the ruling changes to full prayer in this case
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, in which the fasting ruling is being asked about
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the ten-day period that determines the change in travel ruling
key_terms.فَأَتِمَّ: perform in full, without shortening the prayer
key_terms.فَقَصِّرْ: shorten the prayer as a traveler

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler pray full salat and fast instead of shortening prayer and breaking the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for a traveler entering a town: if one intends to stay ten days, the prayer is performed in full; otherwise it is shortened. It also links the rulings of prayer and fasting in travel, establishing that the one who shortens prayer also breaks the fast until the legal condition changes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1269 – Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb reported from Imam Abu Abdullah (as) that He said:

"If you enter a town and intend to stay there for ten days, then you must perform the full prayer as soon as you arrive. But if you intend to stay for less than ten days, you should shorten the prayer. If you keep saying 'Tomorrow I will leave' and 'The day after tomorrow' without deciding to stay for ten days, then you continue to shorten the prayer until it reaches a month ; after a month, you should perform the full prayer."

He (the narrator) said: "I asked: If I enter a town on the first day of Ramadan and I do not intend to stay for ten days, what should I do?"
Imam (as) replied: "Shorten your prayer and break your fast."

He (the narrator) asked: "If I continue in this state, always saying 'Tomorrow' or 'The day after tomorrow,' should I break the fast for the entire month and continue to shorten my prayers?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes, it is one rule: If you shorten your prayer, you break your fast, and if you break your fast, you shorten your prayer."
